title: Meenakshi Sundareswarar Temple, Madurai
summary: The Meenakshi Sundareswarar temple in Madurai, Tamil Nadu, covers about 65,000 square metres and was substantially expanded under Thirumalai Nayak (1623–55). Its four outer gateways are nine-storey gopurams, the tallest being the south tower at 170 feet 6 inches with 1,511 sudhai figures.

uncertainty.note: The Madurai district site says the temple was substantially expanded during the regime of Thirumalai Nayak (1623-55 AD); the building of the south tower itself is not dated on opened pages.

where.modern_name: Meenakshi Amman Temple, Madurai, Tamil Nadu, India
where.historical_name: Sri Meenakshi Sundareswarar Temple, Madurai (Nayak period)

importance.justification: The Madurai district site describes five massive gateways around the two shrines in a complex of 65,000 square metres.

reviewer_note: No model: the south gopuram height (170 ft 6 in, nine storeys) is stated on one page but no plan dimension for it was found. Shape would be stepped_pyramid. The two sources are both government sites; the district site (not the Melur page) gives the 1623-55 expansion and the 65,000 sq m area. Start/end are the expansion reign, not a construction date for the tower. Melur page lists 12 gopurams; district page says five gateways.
